text.en: Mechanist, Elite Operator of Rhodes Island. He leads the R&D, manufacturing, and maintenance of Rhodes Island's weaponry, equipment, engineering facilities, and experimental apparatus, providing essential hardware support for operators across all departments.
text.zh: 机械师，罗德岛精英干员，主导罗德岛的武器装备、工程设施及实验器材的研发、制造及维护工作，为罗德岛各部门干员提供必要的硬件支持。

text.en:
Imaging tests show fuzzy organ outlines and abnormal shadows in the thoracic cavity. Originium granule tests inside circulatory system are abnormal, showing signs of infection. Infected at this stage.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 5%
Traces of Originium crystals can be found on Operator Mechanist's skin.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17 u/L
Operator Mechanist strictly follows the most standard protective procedures, and rarely removes his jumpsuit even off duty.

"Now you know how dangerous mechanical engineering as a hobby can be."
— Mechanist
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】5%
干员机械师体表有少量源石结晶分布。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.17u/L
干员机械师严格遵守最标准的防护流程，甚至在非工作场合也极少脱下工作服。

“现在你知道机械工程是多危险的爱好了。”
——机械师

text.en:
Mechanist almost never takes off his jumpsuit.
Of course, it's not like anyone really wants to look at his weed-like hair or his eyes, varying in size due to sleep deprivation, but we still feel more or less perplexed when he sits down at the dining table in his jumpsuit.
"For the convenience of plunging into work at any moment" was our initial guess. It is not hard to imagine how desperate a person who has just conceived a brilliant inspiration would feel if he found himself forced to complete a tedious set of jumpsuit-wearing procedures at the laboratory entrance.
However, with Mechanist's skills, building a device to help him put on and take off his jumpsuit quickly is not difficult—at least not difficult enough to make someone willing to endure all the inconveniences of wearing a jumpsuit all the time.
Later we learned that he wasn't "enduring" any inconvenience at all.
Inconvenient mobility? The hidden wheels and thrusters on the soles of his shoes say otherwise.
Too hot to wear? The built-in air conditioner, fans, and cooling patches solve the problem.
What if you need an itch scratched? There are two small mechanical arms in the jumpsuit, front and back, moving up and down along guide rails to reach every inch of skin except the soles of the feet.
And what if you need to show your face? Everyone should appreciate the scrolling display screens he sewed into his jumpsuit displaying vulgar Colombian slang, which he used when he returned to Columbia after many years and his mission happened to require him to enter the headquarters of Wolter-Cochinsky.
This layer of jumpsuit turned many problems into the situations Mechanist is best at solving—situations that can be solved by mechanical means.
If you praise him for this, he will politely indicate that he is simply doing things his own way. You won't see his expression, but you can hear the small mechanical arm inside the jumpsuit scratching his head for him.
text.zh:
机械师几乎从来不会脱下他的工作服。
当然，不是说有谁真的想看他杂草一般的头发，或因缺乏睡眠而时大时小的眼睛，但当他穿着工作服坐上饭桌时，我们多多少少还是会感到疑惑。
“为了方便随时投入工作”是我们最初的猜想。不难想象，一个刚刚萌生出绝妙灵感的人，如果发现自己不得不在实验室门口完成一整套繁琐的工作服穿戴流程，会有多么绝望。
但以机械师的技术，打造一套能帮他快速穿脱工作服的装置，并不是难事——至少没难到会让人甘愿忍受一直穿着工作服带来的种种不便。
后来我们才知道，他根本没有在“忍受”任何不便。
行动不便？鞋底的暗轮和喷气罐不这么认为。
穿着太热？内置的空调、风扇和降温贴会解决问题。
需要挠痒怎么办？工作服里前后各有一只小机械手，沿导轨上下移动，能挠到除脚底外的每一寸皮肤。
需要露脸又怎么办？所有人都该欣赏欣赏他时隔多年重回哥伦比亚，任务又恰好需要他出入沃尔沃特科钦斯基的总部时，他缝进工作服里的那些能够滚动显示哥伦比亚粗口的显示屏。
这一层工作服，把许多问题都转化成了机械师最擅长解决的情况——可以用机械手段解决的情况。
如果你因此而夸奖他，他会礼貌地表示他只是在按自己的方式做事罢了。你不会看见他的表情，但你能听到工作服里的小机械手替他挠头的声音。

text.en:
When Mechanist first appeared at our gatherings, he was not yet an Elite Operator.
Those weren't our best times; even when holding a gathering, few people could muster up any joy. You could tell from Misery's face—he would feel sorry for it, but every time he felt pessimistic about things, he would still wear that expression... as if everyone's days were numbered. Raidian would sometimes make "Little Tree" and "Little Ax" hold hands and spin around the table in time with the rhythm, but she used to dance herself. Logos would occasionally still try to amuse everyone with his weird incantations, but he was also very careful to avoid pulling off untimely pranks.
All that was left was the radio playing.
Right at that moment, Mechanist walked through us unconcernedly with his toolbox, and began to fiddle with the thermometer-like device on the wall. That was also one of the gadgets he brought from Columbia, but it seemed to keep breaking down. Every time we came to this gathering, we could see him fixing it.
He started tapping away, and the lyrics on the radio became indistinct, drawing attention instead to many other sounds, like Rhodes Island grinding over the gravel beneath us.
"Which of you on earth is alternating between generating heat and refrigeration?" he suddenly turned around to ask.
Logos looked sheepishly at the flask in his hand, half of which was frozen and the other half still burning.
"Thermodynamics preserve us," he muttered, tossing over a roll of insulation cloth.
"Our time isn't up yet," I looked at him, and suddenly blurted out unprovoked, "At least that guy is still fixing his stuff."
Everyone laughed.
— Ace

It was only after Mechanist joined that we gradually began to develop the habit of organizing various games and competitions.
He was a better hitter than many Rim Billiton natives, and better at imitating song and dance vaudeville acts than many Lateranians. He knew every brand of cigarette card and their corresponding betting rules, and was proficient in the puzzle games published in science fiction magazines. How he used these methods to please investors in the past, we do not know; but the way he skillfully used these things to please himself was witnessed by all. More often, he didn't mind creating a set of absurd rules of his own—the paperclip fencing tournament or the non-burnt potato cooking contest—and dragging everyone into his chaotic gambling den.
Depending on the timing of the gathering, we would cry, laugh, argue, and fall silent, but Mechanist was always doing the same thing. If we weren't in the mood to play with him, he would be with the structural principles; if three people were needed, he would add the mechanical arm behind him.
When the gambling ended and the alcohol had fully dispersed in his body, he would begin to write poetry—writing poetry like throwing a physics monograph into a crucible and stirring it. His recent poetry ended like this:
"Whoever exhibits continuous symmetry in the flux of time, the conserved quantity in their life is life itself."
He often uninvitedly translated my words, and I should occasionally translate his poetry. Like a farmer whose rules of life are demarcated by the timing of sowing, the method of sewing, and the craft of slaughtering Originium Slugs, who will not doubt his life because of any drastic changes on this earth, a person whose rules of life will never be broken will never lose the meaning of his life.
I should perhaps add another joke: Mechanist never realizes he is such a person.
This indeed gives all of us peace of mind. Occasionally, we would all unprovoked blurt out this sentence—
"Our time isn't up yet, at least Mechanist is still reciting his poetry."
— Logos
text.zh:
机械师最早出现在我们的聚会上时，他还不是精英干员。
那不算是我们最好过的时候，哪怕在开聚会也没几个人开心得起来，从Misery脸上就看得出——他会为此感到抱歉，但每次对事情感到悲观的时候，他还是会露出那种……好像所有人都命不久矣的眼神。Raidian有时会让“小树”和“小轴”牵起手，合着拍子在桌上旋转两圈，但她原来是会自己上场跳舞的。Logos偶尔还是会尝试用他那些怪异的咒言逗乐大伙儿，但他也在很小心地避免搞出太不合时宜的恶作剧。
剩下的，就只有收音机在响。
就在那种时候，机械师若无其事地提着工具箱从我们中间穿过去，开始折腾墙上那个温度表似的装置。那也是他从哥伦比亚带来的玩意之一，但似乎一直在出故障，每次我们来这聚会，都能看见他来修。
他开始敲敲打打，收音机里的歌词就听不清了，反倒叫人能注意到很多别的动静，像是罗德岛在我们身下碾过砂石的声音。
“你们之中到底是谁在一会儿产热一会儿制冷？”他突然转头来问。
Logos不好意思地看了看手上那壶一半结了冰，一半还在燃烧的酒。
“热力学在上。”他嘟哝着甩过来一卷隔热布。
“日子还没到头呢，”我看着他，忽然没来由地冒出了这么一句，“至少那家伙还在修他的东西。”
大家都笑了。
——Ace

机械师加入后，我们才逐渐开始有了组织各式游戏和比赛的习惯。
他是个比许多雷姆必拓人都更出色的击球选手，也比许多莱塔尼亚人更擅长模仿歌舞杂耍的桥段。他认得每个品牌的香烟卡和它们对应的下注规则，也精通那些科幻杂志上刊登的解谜游戏。他过去是如何通过这些方式取悦投资人的，我们不得而知；但他熟练地用这些东西取悦自己的模样，我们有目共睹。更多时候，他不介意自创一套荒诞的规则——回形针击剑擂台赛或是土豆不糊锅烹炒大赛——然后把所有人拖进他的混沌赌局。
取决于聚会的时机，我们会哭、会笑、会吵闹、会沉默，但机械师永远在做同样的事。如果我们没心情同他一起玩，他便同结构性原理一起；若是需要三人，就再加上他身后的机械臂。
待到赌局结束，酒精也在他的身体里充分地晕开，他便会开始作诗——如同把物理学专著扔进坩埚搅拌一般地作诗。他最近的诗作如是结尾：
“谁在时间的流变中连续对称，谁生命中的守恒量就是生命本身。”
他常常不请自来地翻译我的话，我也该偶尔翻译一次他的诗。如同平生的规则都是由播种的时机、缝纫的方法和宰杀瘤兽的手艺划定的农人，不会因这片大地上的任何剧变而去怀疑自己的人生，一个生活的规则永远不会被打破的人，他生命的意义也永远不会丧失。
我或许该再补充一个笑话：机械师从来意识不到自己就是这样的人。
这确实令我们所有人感到安心。偶尔，我们都会没来由地冒出这么一句——
“日子还没到头呢，至少机械师还在念他的诗。”
——逻各斯

text.en:
This is my fifth year working at the Patent Office.
My daughter said at school again that she wants to do my job when she grows up, and her teacher came to tell me, so I could only offer as much sincere praise as I could. After all, next time, I'll have to ask the teacher to distribute our questionnaires to the whole class.
Every day's work unfolds in a capsule experimental cabin of less than ten square meters. The technical department sends the filtered patents to our hands, and we, "like little children who just got new toys," apply these technologies to all occasions we can think of. Having obtained the anti-vibration bearings of mobility scooters, why not try using them for the rotating shaft of a cotton candy machine?
The questionnaires come in handy this way. The knowledge brought from the Institute of Technology is put aside, and we first have to understand all possible needs that might exist in this country. Heavens, I even know the "class division" of elementary school students comparing stationery.
It is said that we are turning a patent that perhaps no one will ever pay for into ten or twenty "applied patents" that are bound to be put into production and make a profit. Of course, the ownership of these "applied patents" has nothing to do with the inventor of the original patent, nor with us—they belong to Columbia.
— A researcher at the Colombian Intellectual Property and Patent Office

Resolution passed, and power poured into the Patent Office like a breaching dam. Let the Administration deal with objects, the Patent Office confiscates ideas.
Standard equipment for a Patent Office investigator includes two ballpoint pens, a dozen patent application forms, and a portable door-breacher. With these, they can precisely locate all technical designs not certified by the Patent Office. Unauthorized production? Illegal. Selling blueprints? Illegal. Just using it yourself? There is potential legal risk.
All truly valuable designs must become patents, after which the researchers of the Patent Application Department can multiply and transform new application methods based on them. As for whether inventors actually need the "protection" of patents, it doesn't matter.
One can imagine how much dissatisfaction this resolution triggered when it was just passed. The Patent Office urgently needed to handle a case with enough deterrent force to emphasize their authority.
Wolter-Cochinsky sent a suitable victim, an Aegir engineer who was too obsessed with maintaining his own work and fell out with them. His studio was turned upside down; everything except the designs delivered to the company—those he tried to produce privately for profit, those he gave to his alma mater as teaching aids, and those he used for himself—were confiscated, and he was heavily fined.
Of course, the Patent Office failed to confiscate much in the end, and that Aegir fled with his blueprints to an overseas medical enterprise. But thanks to this, the Patent Office was able to wildly spread rumors that his identity was suspicious and his motives impure, thereby substantiating the justice of the confiscation work.

[An Application for Resignation from the Ship]
Once the adaptive temperature control system is officially put into use on this ship, I will return to Columbia.
Thanks to your esteemed company, all the technologies I brought have been applied reasonably, which means the purpose of my coming here has been fully achieved.
I am aware that returning to Columbia is a dangerous thing for me, but my intuition drives me to focus on the other side of things.
Many people compare the country to a machine, either to state political claims or to hurl political criticism. But after this time, I can indeed clearly feel—
Columbia is a machine.
I still won't give it half a shred of recognition, but its operating logic... has that pure rationality and efficiency unique to machinery. Whether I am a victim of it does not affect this point. I don't like conspiracy theories, but if someone now says that the operation of this country is fundamentally driven by a machine, I wouldn't be surprised.
I am curious.

This application is pinned under Mechanist's workbench and was never submitted to the HR Department.
text.zh:
这是我在专利局工作的第五个年头了。
女儿又在学校说长大了想做我这份工作，她的老师来告诉我，我也只好尽可能真诚地夸上两句。毕竟下次，我还要拜托老师给全班学生发放我们的调查问卷。
每天的工作在一个不到十平米的胶囊式实验舱里展开。技术部门把筛选出的专利送到我们手里，由我们“像刚拿到新玩具的小孩子一样”，把这些技术用在我们能想到的一切场合。拿到的是老年代步车的防颠簸轴承，为什么不试试用来做棉花糖机的转轴呢？
调查问卷就是这样派上用场的。从理工学院带来的知识都放在一边，我们得先来了解一下这个国家可能存在的一切需求。天，我甚至知道小学生攀比文具的“阶级划分”。
上面说，我们是在把一项也许永远没人买单的专利，变成十项、二十项一定能投产、获利的“应用专利”。当然，这些“应用专利”的所有权，和原始专利的发明者无关，和我们也无关——它们属于哥伦比亚。
——哥伦比亚思想产权与专利局的一位研究员

决议通过，权力像决堤般涌入专利局。让管理局去对付物件吧，专利局收缴的是想法。
一位专利局缉查员的标准装备是两支圆珠笔、一打专利申请表，以及一个便携破门器。凭这些，他就可以精准地找出所有未经专利局认证的技术设计。私自投产？违法。出售图纸？违法。只是自己用？存在潜在的违法风险。
一切真正有价值的设计都必须成为专利，那之后，专利应用部的研究员们才好在它们的基础上，成倍地变出新的应用方式。至于发明者是不是真的需要对专利的“保护”，无关紧要。
可以想见这项决议在刚通过时引发了多少不满。专利局迫切地需要办一个足够有震慑力的案子，来强调他们的权威。
沃尔沃特科钦斯基送来了一个合适的受害者，一个太执着于维护自己的作品，以至于和他们闹翻了脸的埃拉菲亚工程师。他的工作室被翻了个底朝天，除了交付给公司的设计，其他的一切——他试图私自投产获利的那些、他送给母校用作教具的那些，还有他给自己用的那些——将被悉数收缴，他也被处以高额罚金。
当然，专利局最终没能收缴到什么，那个埃拉菲亚带着他的图纸逃到了一个境外医疗企业。但也得益于此，专利局才能大肆传扬他身份可疑、动机不纯，借此坐实了收缴工作的正义性。

【一封离舰申请书】
等到自适应温控系统也在这艘船上正式投入使用，我就回哥伦比亚。
感谢贵司，我带来的所有技术都得到了合理的运用，这意味着我来此的目的已经完满达成了。
我清楚回哥伦比亚对我来说是件危险事，但我的直觉在驱使我关注事情的另一方面。
很多人把国家比作机器，要么是为了声明政治主张，要么是为了抛出政治批判。但这次之后，我确实能清晰地感受到——
哥伦比亚是一台机器。
我依然不会对它有半分认可，但它的运作逻辑……有着那种独属于机械的纯粹理性和效率。我是不是其中的受害者，都不影响这一点。我不喜欢阴谋论，但如果现在有人说这个国家的运作在根基上确实是由一台机器推动的，我不会感到奇怪。
我很好奇。

这封申请书被压在机械师的工作台下，从未被递交给人事部。

text.en:
[Excerpt from Unobjective Resume, p.04]
Mechanist did think about leaving Rhodes Island to return to Columbia. At that time, he didn't know Whitesmith yet.
Whitesmith approached him of her own accord. Mechanist's first words at the time were to ask her why she didn't replace her wheelchair with an automated one, when she clearly had the ability to build one.
Tacit understanding between geniuses, I guess. He didn't need to know her to tell she had molten iron in her veins, and she didn't need to have met him to figure out he had gears in his brain. Whitesmith knew her own physical condition and understood that the Rhodes Island workshop needed a successor, and Mechanist arrived just in time.
She didn't expect Mechanist to be extremely unskilled at this job. When he first took over the equipment maintenance and manufacturing work for Elite Operators, not a single one of his works could be used properly. The compound bow he painstakingly polished for three days fell apart in Stormeye's hands in three minutes, and the flying bowstring almost severed half of Stormeye's horn.
The next day, a plastic basket appeared at the door of Mechanist's workshop, containing a bottle of whiskey. For a while after that, Mechanist never left the workshop, and a bottle of wine would appear in the basket at the door every day. Mechanist never drank during working hours, and he said these were saved until he solved the problem. When that time came, he would drink all the wine he wanted to drink in these days in one breath without missing the chance.
It's not hard to understand why he was so obsessed. Even though he kept his helmet on, everyone could tell that the truth he had believed in for more than twenty years had shattered at Rhodes Island. He couldn't understand why his perfect designs, which seemed to be the embodiment of physical laws, appeared so clumsy in the hands of Elite Operators. He iterated his designs at a rate of five drafts a day; of course, the result still failed to meet his wishes.
Whether taking over someone else's engineering or adjusting machinery based on humans was still too unfamiliar to him at that time. He didn't understand that those unruly Elite Operators actually only needed a little quirky "flaw".

[Excerpt from Unobjective Resume, p.11]
By that time Whitesmith's condition was already very poor, and the workshop was being managed entirely by Mechanist. But one day, she suddenly said she wanted to forge something again.
She lit the forge for the first time in a long time, originally just wanting to repair someone's weapon, but Mechanist told her that all weapon repair requests had been processed. For this final time, he hoped Whitesmith's forge would burn only for herself.
All the equipment she needed was modified by Mechanist to just the right degree, requiring manual operation for each step, but requiring only very small movements for each operation. Even Whitesmith, who had difficulty moving her arms at the time, was able to operate it.
A small pendant, Whitesmith forged it from day to night, and from night to day, but what she lacked least was sincerity and perseverance. Mechanist watched from the side all along, knowing that no matter how long it took, it could only be completed by her own hands.
Finally, when the pendant was finally finished, Mechanist shaved off a facet of the gem. The glowing light reflected by this gem would never fall perfectly in its exact center, but this way, it looked more like Whitesmith's eyes.
After this, Whitesmith's forge could never be lit again. That night, Mechanist drank all the wine at the door of the workshop by himself.

"When we first met, I asked her why she didn't replace her wheelchair with an automated one. She said, because her hands could still move.
"This is the reason I stay at Rhodes Island."
— Mechanist
text.zh:
【非客观履历节选，p.04】
机械师确实想过要离开罗德岛回哥伦比亚。那时候，他还不认识Whitesmith。
Whitesmith主动找上了他。当时机械师的第一句话，是问她为什么不把轮椅换成自动的，她明明有能力打造一辆。
天才之间的默契吧，我猜。他不需要认识她就看得出她血管里都是熔铁，她也不需要见过他就能想到他脑子里都是齿轮。Whitesmith清楚自己的身体状况，也明白罗德岛的工坊需要一个继任者，而机械师来得正是时候。
她没有料到，机械师极其不擅长这份工作。最初接手精英干员的装备维护和制造工作时，他的作品没有一件能正常使用。他精心打磨三天的复合弓，在Stormeye手里三分钟就四分五裂，崩飞的弓弦险些切断了Stormeye的半只角。
第二天，机械师的工作间门口多了一个塑料筐，里面放着一瓶威士忌。之后的一阵子，机械师再没离开过工作间，而门口的筐子里每天都会多出一瓶酒。机械师在工作时间从不喝酒，他说，这些是留到他把问题解决之后再喝的。到时候，他要一口气把这些天里想喝但没机会喝的酒都补上。
不难理解他为什么如此执着。哪怕他一直戴着头盔大家也都看得出，他二十多年来深信不疑的真理碎在了罗德岛。他不能明白自己那些仿佛物理法则化身的完美设计，为什么在精英干员们手里显得如此拙劣。他以每天五稿的速度迭代自己的设计，当然，结果依然没能如他所愿。
不论是接手别人的工程，还是以人为基准去调整机械，对于那时的他都还太陌生。他还不明白，那些不甚循规蹈矩的精英干员，需要的其实都只是一点古怪的“瑕疵”。

【非客观履历节选，p.11】
那时候Whitesmith的状况已经很差了，工坊已经是由机械师在全权打理。但某天，她忽然说想再锻造点什么。
她久违地点起了锻炉，原本只是想替谁修修武器，但机械师告诉她，所有武器修理需求都已经处理完了。最后这一次，他希望Whitesmith的锻炉只为她自己而燃。
她要用的所有设备，机械师都改造到了一个恰到好处的程度，每个步骤都还需要手动操作，但每项操作都只需要很小幅度的动作就能完成。哪怕是那时候连活动手臂都很费力的Whitesmith，也能操作得了。
一枚小小的挂坠，Whitesmith从白天锻到黑夜，又从黑夜锻到白天，但她最不缺的就是真诚和毅力。机械师从始至终在一旁看着，他知道这件事不论要花费多久，都只能由她亲手完成。
最后，当挂坠终于完工，机械师削去了宝石上的一个面。这颗宝石映出的辉光再也不会完美地落在它的正中央，但这样，它看起来才更像Whitesmith的眼睛。
在此之后，Whitesmith的锻炉再也没能燃起火焰。那天晚上，机械师一个人喝光了工作间门口所有的酒。

“第一次见面的时候，我问她为什么不把轮椅换成自动的。她说，因为她的手还能动。
“这就是我留在罗德岛的理由。”
——机械师

text.en:
Yes, this is structural principle, Mechanist's proudest work.
It is far from as cute as it looks. We rarely use "extremely strong territorial awareness" to describe a machine, but applying it to structural principles is truly most appropriate. The engineering department's vehicle parking lot originally had no assigned parking spaces; whether it was Bagpipe's small tractor, Earthspirit's sidecar motorcycle, or those operation platforms, they could park wherever they wanted—until the structural principle came into being. No one knew how it selected that parking space, but as long as anyone approached its parking space, it would stiffen its neck and adopt an aggressive posture to drive away the intruder.
Mechanist refuses to admit when sober that structural principle has any personality to speak of as a machine, but everyone knows why it has this personality. Just as he always fails to realize that his poems are all depicting himself, he also fails to realize how similar structural principle is to him.
Yes, Mechanist is a person with "extremely strong territorial awareness". Initially, his "territory" only contained unshakeable physical laws and all those proud works of his that he allowed no one else to touch. But now, he can no longer tell what is in his "territory"; there are more people he cares about in it, more principles he recognizes, and perhaps more things he wants to accomplish.
Since he could disregard consequences to defy the federal government's penalty order to protect his work back then, now, for the people and things he cares about, he will surely not step back half a step.

"Just like how he set twenty defense programs for structural principle?"
"Just like structural principle stiffening its neck to guard its parking space."
text.zh:
是的，这就是结构性原理，机械师最骄傲的作品。
它远不像看起来那么可爱。我们很少用“领地意识极强”描述一台机器，但用在结构性原理身上确实再合适不过。工程部的载具停放库原本没有车位归属之分，不论是风笛的小型拖拉机、地灵的偏三轮摩托，还是那几个自律作业平台，都是想停哪就停哪——直到结构性原理问世。谁也不知道它是怎样选中了那个车位，但只要有人靠近它的车位，它就会梗起脖子，摆出攻击姿态驱赶来者。
机械师在清醒时拒绝承认结构性原理作为机械有任何性格可言，但所有人都知道它为什么是这个性格。就像他总是意识不到自己的诗作都在描绘自己，他也不会意识到结构性原理与他有多么相像。
是的，机械师就是个“领地意识极强”的人。最初，他的“领地”里只有不可撼动的物理法则，和他所有那些绝不许别人染指的骄傲作品。但如今，他已经说不清他的“领地”里都有些什么了，那里面多了些他在意的人，多了些他认可的道理，或许也多了些他想做到的事。
既然当初他能为了保护自己的作品不顾后果地违抗联邦政府的处罚令，那现在，为了他在意的人和事，他想必也不会退让半步。

“就像他给结构性原理设置了二十道防御程序？”
“就像结构性原理梗着脖子守护自己的车位。”
